page: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v6 is a low-memory compute instance within the general-purpose virtual machine lineup, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8).

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread compute capabilities, with Geekbench single-core performance scoring 2104.0 and gzip compression achieving 31.3 GB/sec, placing both in the upper tier of tested instances. The presence of Intel AMX extensions delivers strong performance in low-parameter language tasks, demonstrated by small 135M model inference text generation reaching 348.14 tokens/sec. Multi-threaded evaluations, including Geekbench multi-core (13049.0) and PassMark CPU (26491.39), align with median expectations for 16-vCPU hosts.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the constrained memory profile alongside the absence of bundled local storage. Because no local NVMe drives are provisioned, workloads rely exclusively on remote Azure storage volumes. This design provides cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks by eliminating expenses associated with unused memory capacity or attached ephemeral scratch disks.

Microsoft Azure D16ls_v6 is suited for compute-focused applications that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Appropriate deployment targets include web application servers, CI/CD compilation runners, microservices architectures, data preprocessing, and CPU-based lightweight AI inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. There is no bundled local storage, requiring attached network disks for file persistence, and no discrete GPUs are present. Benchmarks show upper-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong AMX-driven inference execution on small language models, while multi-threaded integer and memory operations place in the median tier. The instance offers resource efficiency for CPU-intensive systems that do not need large working memory footprints, making it suitable for software compilation, web serving, microservices, and targeted inferencing tasks.
